main_math: For fused weights proportional to (v_p M_qt-v_q M_pt)^2, alpha_i=v_i^2+||(I-vv^T)M row i||^2/Z. Moving a heavy original coordinate h to the arbitrary bank gives |lambda'|Z'=|lambda|Z(1-alpha_h) and conditions the fused law on avoiding h. Two transfers yield either a density bound with retained mass >=1/4 or >3/4 fused mass meeting at most two original coordinates.
partner_application: On account03/B06 r39, Z>=x2>11907/1048576. For |lambda|>=1 the diffuse exit gives ||p_Q||inf<74.509547612; otherwise <=2 physical rows meet fused mass >0.008516550064.
counterexample_to_intermediate: v=e1, M=[[0,0],[1,0],[0,1]] has 100% fused mass incident to coordinate 1 but physical cross row 1 is zero. With lambda=1 the genuine target Q=X1^2+2X2Y1+2X3Y2 has spectrum {1,1,1,-1,-1} and is paid by exact-rank-two crossing plus the pinned half-Riesz square peel: ||p_Q||inf<=4sqrt2.
next_step: Quantitatively split the <=2-row fused concentration certificate into true hub-partner volume versus localized-square volume, then apply the current two-hub transverse-square/projected-crossing receiver or the localized-square rank-two half-Riesz peel while retaining the complete cross tail.
